statement: Let $R$ be the counterclockwise rotation by $100^\circ$ about the origin and let $S$ be the reflection across the $x$-axis. Define $T(Q) = S(R(Q))$: rotate, then reflect. Start with $P_0 = (\cos 30^\circ, \sin 30^\circ)$ and let $P_k = T(P_{k-1})$ for $k \ge 1$. Then $P_{2027} = (\cos\theta, \sin\theta)$ for exactly one $\theta$ with $0 \le \theta < 360$, measured in degrees. What is $\theta$?

choices.misconception: I added up all the rotations, 2027 times 100 degrees, which is 20 degrees mod 360, and added that to 30 degrees, ignoring the reflections entirely.
I applied the maps in the wrong order, reflecting first and then rotating, so one step sent 30 degrees to -30 degrees and then to 70 degrees.
I saw that T undoes itself on the second step, so P_2027 = T(P_0), but then I only applied the rotation and forgot the reflection.
I combined all the rotations into a single 20 degree turn to reach 50 degrees, then applied one reflection because 2027 is odd, getting -50 degrees.

hints: Track what one step does to the angle of a point on the unit circle.
Rotation adds $100^\circ$ to the angle and reflection negates it. Work out what two steps in a row do to an angle $\alpha$.
One step sends $\alpha$ to $-(\alpha + 100)$. Apply it twice: $-(-(\alpha+100) + 100) = \alpha$. So $T$ has period $2$.

solutions.reliable: For a point at angle $\alpha$ on the unit circle, $R$ sends it to angle $\alpha + 100$ and $S$ negates the angle, so $T$ sends $\alpha$ to $-\alpha - 100$. Applying $T$ twice gives $-(-\alpha - 100) - 100 = \alpha$, so $T \circ T$ is the identity. Since $2027$ is odd, $P_{2027} = T(P_0)$, which has angle $-30 - 100 = -130 \equiv 230$. So $\theta = 230$. Check: $P_1$ is at $230^\circ$, $P_2$ is at $-(230 + 100) = -330 \equiv 30^\circ$, back to the start. The idea: a rotation followed by a reflection is itself a reflection, so it has period 2.
solutions.elegant: A rotation followed by a reflection reverses orientation and fixes the origin, so $T$ is a reflection across some line through the origin. Every reflection is its own inverse, so odd powers of $T$ equal $T$, and $T(P_0)$ sits at $-(30 + 100) = -130$, that is $230^\circ$.
